Case Study // Full Stack Web Platform

KINO VIBE

Project Spec Personal Movie Review & Tier Ranking Platform for Blockbuster Cinema

Engineered for film lovers and blockbuster cinema enthusiasts who want more nuance than generic star ratings. Combines a 4-pillar scoring formula, personal bias modifiers, live TMDB API metadata syncing, and automatic S-to-F tier classification.

01 / Overview

Executive Summary

Conventional film rating platforms rely heavily on flat 5-star or single 1–10 scores. For high-spectacle modern cinema and summer blockbusters — such as Dune: Part Two, Mad Max: Fury Road, or Top Gun: Maverick — a single number collapses distinct cinematic achievements. A film might exhibit world-class VFX, stunt choreography, and auditory punch, yet feature straightforward narrative beats.

KinoVibe was architected as a dedicated platform to break past single-score compromises. By scoring films independently across Story, Visuals, Action, and Fun, factoring in user-defined Bias Modifiers (e.g., IMAX experience, director loyalty, plot pacing), and leveraging live TMDB metadata, KinoVibe dynamically auto-organizes your cinematic library into an S-to-F Tier List.

02 / Challenges

Engineering Hurdles

Building a rich, responsive film catalog and rating tool required addressing several distinct frontend and architectural challenges:

▶ Live TMDB Autocomplete & Image Caching: Seamlessly querying The Movie Database API v3 with input debouncing, preventing rate-limit throttling while rendering instant high-res poster and backdrop previews.
▶ Mathematical Score Balancing: Creating a responsive slider formula that computes base criteria, incorporates dynamic positive and negative biases, and ensures final ratings stay within a strict 0.0–10.0 boundary.
▶ Automated Tier Bucket Engine: Dynamically bucketing and rendering movie entries across 7 tiers (S, A, B, C, D, E, F) without manual drag-and-drop friction or layout shifts.
▶ Cloud Sync with Row-Level Security: Integrating Supabase PostgreSQL authentication and RLS policies so individual film logs and custom biases remain isolated to each user.
03 / Architecture

System Architecture & Formulas

The application was built using modular ES6+ JavaScript, CSS3 with a cinematic dark palette, Supabase as the serverless PostgreSQL backend, and TMDB API v3 for live cinema metadata.

1. The 4-Pillar Scoring Formula

Users grade films on four distinct 0–10 scales:

  • Story: Narrative structure, screenwriting, dialogue, and emotional stakes.
  • Visuals: Cinematography, VFX, production design, and color grading.
  • Action: Choreography, practical stunts, tension, and set pieces.
  • Fun: Entertainment momentum, pure popcorn factor, and rewatchability.
// Base & Final Score Algorithm
Base Score = (Story + Visuals + Action + Fun) / 4
Final Score = clamp(0.0, 10.0, (Story + Visuals + Action + Fun + Total Biases) / 4)

2. Dynamic Tier Classification Table

S TIER: ≥ 9.0
Masterpiece / Absolute Kino
A TIER: 8.0 – 8.9
Great Cinema
B TIER: 7.0 – 7.9
Good & Entertaining
C TIER: 6.0 – 6.9
Decent Watch

3. TMDB API Integration Pipeline

When a user types a movie title into the review creator, a debounced query initiates an asynchronous call to TMDB's search endpoint. Upon selecting a title, the system automatically populates release year, director credits, genres, backdrop hero art, poster thumbnails, and synopsis, cutting movie entry time down to seconds.
